source_text: You can be granted 1 click under the new system and it needs to be pushed through end to end

fragments.text: You can be granted 1 click under the new system
it needs to be pushed through end to end

reply_text:
Understood: one click, and that one run gets pushed through to the end. I'm not firing it yet, because the debugger it depends on is still being built.

**What "end to end" means for this click.** The one run reaches a reviewed, grounded change, with a terminal receipt naming its commit. There is no second click. If the run fails at a phase, it waits there. I record the failure as an incident and assign it to the component owner. The repair is reviewed and loaded, and the same run continues from that phase.

**What has to be true before I fire it:**

1. **The debugger is loaded and attached.** codex-5 is building it now (`invoke-1790754163381-28861-7fdf23f5`, running). If it needs a new library on the serving JVM's classpath, that may mean a restart, which is your call. I'll bring you that question with their report.
2. **The failure I already know is ahead is handled.** As things stand, this click would select M-descriptive-essay-of-the-stack and the author would refuse for the third time, because the I1–I6 audit is missing. Spending the click to rediscover that would repeat today's mistake. So the author's typed refusal has to be raised and handled first: the refusal is recorded against that attempt, and the run goes back to selection with that attempt excluded. That is controller work for codex-6. It builds on codex-5's mechanism, so it follows their report.

One thing I don't know yet is whether selection can be told to exclude an attempt. If it can't, the selection owner gets a small piece of work as well.

I've recorded the grant and these conditions in the rulings (commit `ab96c12f3`). codex-5's job is parked under `park-f17a3e6f…`; I'll report when it lands.
